description: Money from outside USG: sponsorship, co-hosting, donations, fundraising, tickets, dues, drawings and raffles (Student Handbook 2026-27, Campus Activities, USG web page).

rules.title: In-kind corporate sponsorship
rules.source_text: Corporate Sponsorships can only be in-kind donations and must add value to the RSO or event and may not include monetary donations.
rules.message: A company may sponsor an event in kind (food, products, a venue), if it adds value and the club stays the primary contact, payer and first name on all advertising.
rules.applies_to: A company offering goods or services for an event

rules.title: No cash from corporate sponsors
rules.source_text: Corporate Sponsorships can only be in-kind donations and must add value to the RSO or event and may not include monetary donations.
rules.message: Corporate sponsorship can only be in kind. A company cannot give the club money.
rules.fix_template: Ask the sponsor for goods or services (for example the food) instead of money.
rules.applies_to: A company offering money for an event

rules.title: The club stays primary contact, payer and first name
rules.source_text: The RSO must be the primary contact for Campus Activities, and other campus departments involved in the planning or approval of the event. • The main contact from the RSO must be a current, full-time student and member of the RSO. • The money must be paid by the RSO and not the outside agency for any fees owed to the university. • The RSO must be the primary name listed on all advertisements and promotional materials. • The main contact from the RSO must be present at all meetings, walkthroughs, and day-of event as the primary producer of the event.
rules.message: When a club hosts an event with an outside organization or sponsor, the club must be the primary contact, its main contact must be a current full-time student member who is present at all meetings, walkthroughs and on the day, the club pays all university fees, and the club's name comes first on all advertising.
rules.fix_template: Make the club the payer, the primary contact and the first name on every flyer.
rules.applies_to: An event co-hosted with an outside organization, or with a sponsor

rules.title: The audience must be mainly USC students and alumni
rules.source_text: The primary target audience for the event must be USC students and alumni.
rules.message: When a club hosts an event with an outside organization or sponsor, the main audience must be USC students and alumni.
rules.fix_template: Aim the event and its advertising at USC students and alumni.
rules.applies_to: An event co-hosted with an outside organization, or with a sponsor

rules.title: Co-hosting with another recognized club
rules.source_text: As many RSOs co-sponsor events with other student organizations, departments, and/or outside agencies, it is important to be aware of what constitutes a co-sponsorship.
rules.message: Clubs co-sponsor events with other student organizations, departments and outside agencies; the co-sponsorship conditions apply, a co-host that is not a recognized student organization is not allowed, and every co-host is named in the permit application.
rules.applies_to: Sharing an event and its costs with another club

rules.title: No co-hosting with unrecognized groups
rules.source_text: Co-sponsorships with Unrecognized Student Organizations are strictly prohibited.
rules.message: Co-hosting with a group that is not a recognized student organization is strictly prohibited.
rules.fix_template: Co-host only with a recognized student organization.
rules.applies_to: A co-hosted event

rules.title: Clubs may not bring a business to campus as a vendor
rules.source_text: RSOs may not bring a business to campus as a vendor. Businesses can only come to campus if a pre-existing event is occurring (i.e., the business’s participation in the event cannot be the primary purpose of the event).
rules.message: A club cannot bring a business to campus as a vendor; a business may take part only in an event that exists for its own sake.
rules.fix_template: Remove the vendor sales. A business may take part only in an event that exists for its own purpose.
rules.applies_to: An event with an outside business selling or promoting

rules.title: Outside vendors may not sell on campus without permission
rules.owner_office: Student Life and Trojan Event Services (TES)
rules.source_text: Outside vendors are prohibited from selling on campus without prior permission from one of these departments: • USC Bookstores, (213) 740-4317. • USC Private Events & Conferences, (213) 740-5956. • USC Athletic Department, (213) 740-5200. • Trojan Event Services, (213) 764-4943.
rules.message: Outside vendors may not sell on campus without prior permission from the USC Bookstores, USC Private Events & Conferences, the USC Athletic Department or Trojan Event Services.
rules.fix_template: Get permission for the vendor sales from one of those departments, or remove them.
rules.applies_to: An event where an outside vendor sells to attendees

rules.title: Donations only through the university
rules.source_text: As student organizations recognized by the university, RSOs may solicit and receive tax-deductible contributions through the university (which is exempt from income tax under I.R.C. Section 501(c)(3)). RSOs are required to work with Campus Activities before engaging in any fundraising activities using the university’s tax exempt status (see Sales and Fundraising by RSOs, below).
rules.message: Clubs may solicit and receive tax-deductible donations through the university, working with Campus Activities first.
rules.applies_to: Asking people or organizations for donations

rules.title: Filing for the club's own tax-exempt status loses recognition
rules.source_text: RSOs that file their own application with the IRS or another government agency seeking tax exempt status without the prior approval of Campus Activities will no longer be recognized by the university as a student organization.
rules.message: A club that files for its own tax-exempt status without Campus Activities' approval loses recognition.
rules.fix_template: Do not file without Campus Activities' prior approval; ask them about receiving donations through the university.
rules.applies_to: A plan to register the club as a non-profit

rules.title: Fundraisers and sales, with approval
rules.source_text: Although all RSOs are permitted to fundraise on their own behalf, RSOs may only pursue fundraising activities to benefit their student organization, another RSO, or an outside philanthropic agency or relief effort.
rules.message: Clubs may fundraise for themselves, another club, or a charity or relief effort, after meeting Campus Activities at least 2 weeks before. Item sales need Bookstore approval; cash at the event needs Trojan Event Services and Department of Public Safety approval.
rules.applies_to: A fundraiser, sale or money collection

rules.title: Fundraising and ticket sales are approved case by case
rules.source_section: Sales and Fundraising by RSOs: Process
rules.source_text: Ticket sales as a fundraising activity may not be approved for every event. See Ticket Events/Payment for Services section for more details. v. Other types – Campus Activities, Trojan Event Services and other campus partners may approve the fundraising request based on the event details.
rules.message: Campus Activities, Trojan Event Services and other campus offices decide whether to approve a fundraiser or ticket sales, event by event.
rules.fix_template: Ask Campus Activities early; the meeting is due 2 weeks before the event.
rules.applies_to: An event with fundraising, ticket sales, item sales or money collection

rules.title: No member may profit from fundraising
rules.source_text: No individual student or person(s) may receive any type of benefit or payment in connection with any of these activities, either in the form of money, trade, discounts, and/or any other goods or services.
rules.message: No member or other person may receive money, trade, discounts or goods from the club's fundraising.
rules.fix_template: Remove any payment or benefit to individuals.
rules.applies_to: A fundraiser or sale

rules.title: Ticket sales only to cover the event's costs
rules.source_text: Event tickets or payment for services (performances, activities, etc.) are permissible if approved proceeds from sales will help the RSOs cover expenses for that specific event or activity.
rules.message: Tickets may be sold only to cover that event's own costs. A ticketed event cannot get USG funding.
rules.applies_to: Selling tickets

rules.title: No raffles that require a purchase or donation
rules.source_text: In the State of California, raffles and lotteries are illegal if a person is required to purchase a ticket or make a donation in order to be eligible to win the contest.
rules.message: A raffle that requires buying a ticket or donating is illegal in California.
rules.fix_template: Run a free drawing instead, with the required ticket wording.
rules.applies_to: A prize drawing that requires a purchase or donation

rules.title: Free drawings: the rules California law requires
rules.source_text: Free drawings are legal when rules conforming to the California State Law are followed exactly. These rules are: • The drawing must be in connection with an event or an RSO. • The ticket must have the following information displayed on it: – Date, time, and location of drawing. – Name of sponsors and beneficiary of fundraising. – Donation or purchase of ticket is not required to be eligible to win. – Winner need not be present at drawing (not required but advised). • Free tickets (a minimum of one per person) must be available. • Each solicitor must know that free tickets can be obtained and how to obtain them. • The word “drawing” or “free drawing” is required; the word “raffle” on the ticket or in advertisements should not be used.
rules.message: A drawing must follow these rules exactly: it is tied to an event or the club; each ticket shows the date, time and place of the drawing, the sponsors and beneficiary, that no donation or purchase is needed to win, and (advised) that the winner need not be present; free tickets are available, at least one per person; everyone handing out tickets knows how to get a free one; and it is called a 'drawing' or 'free drawing', never a 'raffle'.
rules.fix_template: Print the required wording on every ticket, offer free tickets, and call it a free drawing.
rules.applies_to: A prize drawing

rules.title: Silent auctions go through University Advancement
rules.source_text: The same rules apply for coordinating a silent auction as would apply for a free drawing. All silent auctions must work with University Advancement.
rules.message: A silent auction follows the free-drawing rules and must be run with University Advancement.
rules.fix_template: Contact Campus Activities to arrange the auction with University Advancement.
rules.applies_to: A silent auction

rules.title: No sponsorship activations
rules.source_text: An activation is any event that brings a non-university affiliated company or business onto campus solely to market its products or services. Often, sponsoring companies will approach RSOs about booking their event on campus, or promoting their brand, in exchange for money or products. The university does not permit RSOs to engage in sponsorship activations. Campus Activities is permitted to approve requests for Sponsorship Activations on behalf of Student Life. USC Student Government (USG & GSG) is the only student-led entity at USC that is permitted to utilize sponsorship activations, in collaboration with Campus Activities, and is limited to booking two sponsorship activations per semester.
rules.message: Clubs cannot host sponsorship activations (a company coming to campus to market itself, for money or products). USC Student Government (USG and GSG) is the only student-led entity that may, with Campus Activities.
rules.fix_template: Decline the activation, or ask the company for an in-kind sponsorship of a club event instead.
rules.applies_to: A company booth, promotion or brand event on campus

rules.title: No brand ambassadors or third-party promoters
rules.source_section: Appendix IX: Advertising, Promotion/Publicity, and Literature Distribution
rules.source_text: The use of third-party promoters, including student brand ambassadors, is strictly prohibited.
rules.message: Third-party promoters, including student brand ambassadors, are strictly prohibited.
rules.fix_template: Remove the brand ambassador or promoter from the plan.
rules.applies_to: Promoting through a brand ambassador or outside promoter

rules.title: Voluntary dues
rules.source_text: Dues may not be required as criteria for any level of membership. While groups may choose to collect dues, dues must not be a requirement for becoming a member or to be associated with specific level of membership (e.g., voting membership or officer).
rules.message: A club may collect dues, but paying them can never be required for any level of membership.
rules.applies_to: Collecting member dues

rules.title: Dues may not be required
rules.source_text: Dues may not be required as criteria for any level of membership. While groups may choose to collect dues, dues must not be a requirement for becoming a member or to be associated with specific level of membership (e.g., voting membership or officer).
rules.message: Dues cannot be a requirement for joining, for voting membership, or for holding office.
rules.applies_to: Membership that requires paying dues

rules.title: Other USC funds: ask USG first
rules.source_section: Frequently Asked Questions: What are other sources of funding besides USG?
rules.source_text: Students have several options for funding, including fundraising, crowdfunding through IgniteSC, membership fees, USC Academic Departments, USC Grants, fellowships or scholarships, programming assemblies and committees, partnering with other RSOs, and receiving donations from donors or USC alumni.
rules.message: Other USC money (academic departments, school councils, programming assemblies, grants) can help, but USG lists funding from another University source as a possible reason to deny a USG application. Ask USG before combining them.
rules.fix_template: Ask USG (usgfunds@usc.edu) before using another USC source for an event USG also funds.
rules.applies_to: Using other USC money for an event
rules.notes: The USG web page recommends other USC sources; the USG guidelines list another University source as a possible denial reason. Shown yellow, never green.
